Bug_Details:
Classes that override equals should also override hashCode. The contract for Object.hashCode states that if two objects are equal, then
calling the hashCode() method on each of the two objects must produce the same
result. Implementing equals() but not hashCode() causes broken behaviour
when trying to store the object in a collection. See Effective Java 3rd Edition §11 for more information and a
discussion of how to correctly implement hashCode().
Bug_Explanation: The class 'Person' overrides the 'equals' method, but does not override the 'hashCode' method. This violation of the equals-hashCode contract causes broken behaviour when trying to store 'Person' objects in a HashSet. The'showBug' method demonstrates this by adding two 'Person' objects with the same name to a HashSet and then printing the size of the HashSet. The expected output is 1, but the actual output is 2 due to the bug.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when the showBug() method in the Person class is called in the testEqualsHashCodeBug() method. The showBug() method adds two Person objects with the same name to a HashSet and then prints the size of the HashSet. The expected output is 1, but the actual output is 2 due to the bug in the Person class not overriding the hashCode() method.
